utterances.text: Is there anything specific about those locations, was there some kind of particular regime there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: For example we would be going towards Dragalic, then at Gradiska we would rest, we would stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, we didn't understand each other. Those places where the exchanges were being conducted was there a special entry and exit regime there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it was normal, we would just go in with a roll call.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the zones where the exchanges were held, were they the UNPAs under the control of the UN?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, you rode on those buses, did you stop anywhere before entering the actual place of exchange?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course we did. I mentioned it a while ago, for example we'd be going to Dragalic and then we had's stop in Gradiska for about a half an hour, approximately. All of those who were on the bus were allowed to get off. I would take them to the washroom and then we would go back, some of them said they would like to have a beer or something like that and those wishes of theirs were fulfilled too and also if they wanted to buy a bit of food or something like that, that's the way it was for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, did Miroslav Tadic travel with you or did he travel separately?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: He travelled separately and I was on the bus, I was invariably on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, what happened at the place where the exchange took place? What was the procedure involved, did these people state their views regarding the exchange yet again before someone else? Could you explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: We would stop there and the buses would park on both sides. All of those who were supposed to be exchanged were on the buses and then they would get off and they would stand in queues or rather a queue and the others did the same. The civilian population, I mean the International Red Cross was there too, and they observed all of that. Then, I would call out people's names, the names of all of those who were on the list. And then I'd say, "Are you going?" And then he would say that he wanted to go. And then he'd go there straight away and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? Where did they go then? Did they state their views to anybody else or only to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: He would apply to the International Red Cross and then he would go over straight to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just let's do this step by step. You would read out the person's name from the list and you would ask this person does he want to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After that, the person who says --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: That he wants to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then he goes where?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: The International Red Cross would listen to all of this but then he would go to the International Red Cross and then he would go back take his things and go over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So he would return again to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: To the bus?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And take his own things.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And go on to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, you are not pausing. It's so much strain on the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, let's do this slowly. What happened to people who would express their wishes to you, who would say to you that they did not want to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Such persons would also say loud and clear that they did not want to go. They would also go to the International Red Cross, but they would also have there the representatives of the other side and they would address these people too and they would tell them also that they did not want to go. So then the person involved would come back to me and say, "What do I do now." And then I would say, "Take your things, if you have any," because I mean, you know, if he was counting on going back anyway and then I'd say go back to the bus and sit in your seat. That was it. Let me just say one more thing. May I? Oh, all right, never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just take it slowly. Let's try to finish with this part. These people would get on to the same bus on which they came?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Came, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now tell me what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was happy. All of us were happy. All of those who said that they wanted to go back to Samac. We were all happy and pleased.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, at these exchanges that you attended, were there several such cases of persons who said that they did not want to go to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course. I know quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a few names to the best of your recollection, a few names as many as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Mladen Borbeli then that Slovenian, then Stipe Vukovic, then this Ivica Kikic and so on. I can't remember everybody now but there were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After returning to Samac, what happened to them, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: They went to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where do they live now?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: They live in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, was the procedure same on the other side with the Serb detainees and civilians who were coming from the other side? Was the procedure identical to the one that you had here? How did these people state their views? What did you manage to see?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Well to tell you the truth, I don't really know because I was not in a position to hear that or see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, on that occasion, did you force anyone to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted people to stay or to come back, not to cross over, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear or see -- do you know whether Miroslav Tadic forced anybody to go to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No way, no way. I don't think that that was in the back of his mind let alone that he actually wanted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we have some assistance from the technical people? I'm informed that the technical people are working on them so we should just wait. Can we start? Yes. I think you have to go back a bit so that you cover, if you have lost anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask my colleague to read this because we have it on the laptop.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will read what we have here on the laptop to recover the transcript. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why don't -- why don't you just repeat the questions? Because it seems to me there is nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, we have a small problem with the transcript?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The last few questions and answers did not enter the transcript so I'm going to repeat them. Mr. Vasovic, did you force anyone to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. Never. Never, never did it cross my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about Miroslav Tadic, did you know, see or hear that Miroslav Tadic forced someone to cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No way. He's not that kind of person to do that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, you told us a while ago that you read these lists of civilians who were stating their views?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was the same thing done with persons who were coming from detention, did they also express their views to the representatives of the International Red Cross et cetera?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, those who came, I mean whoever came came, I didn't go into all of that. I didn't go into whether or not these people expressed their views.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you. I'm asking you whether those persons who came with you on the bus and who were supposed to cross over to the other side and who had been detained in Samac, did they also express their views there. Are they also in the category that you referred to just now that everybody together went to the International Red Cross or was there a difference between them?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Everybody, everybody, I can that everybody went to the Red Cross and expressed their views there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was the procedure identical when the International Red Cross was not there, did somebody come instead of them?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: The commission on both sides. I think that this was truly correct and that all exchanges were indeed carried out properly, quite properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any representatives of the Red Cross from Zupanja or somewhere?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: From Zupanja, there were representatives of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, now I'm going to ask you something else about a different subject and that is Zasavica. Do you know where the village of Zasavica is?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: It is on the right side of Crkvina towards Modrica, towards the town of Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, tell me, what was the population of Zasavica in ethnic terms?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: The population was Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, did you come to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Not exactly every day but perhaps it could even be put that way, even every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, during those days, I mean I'm interested in a longer period of time, so May, June, July, all the way up to say the end of August, 1992, who were mainly the inhabitants of Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Only Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of communication did you have, could they move about unhindered? Did you meet them in town?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they went out. They went into town. It was quite normal in relation to the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did something happen towards the end of August 1992? Did some other people come there in addition to these?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. When that group of Muslims swam across the Sava and the Bosna I think - now I'm not too sure whether it was the Sava or the Bosna - and then their families were brought to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, who did that? Who brought them there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: The police. The police, nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, at that time, were there any restrictions on movement, was there a checkpoint at the entrance into Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: At the small bridge by the entrance into Zasavica there was a small checkpoint where there were guards and they either allowed entry or did not or rather only people who had passes were allowed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, on whose instructions did you go to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: According to the instructions given by the Red Cross, everything I did I did according to the instructions given by the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vasovic, specifically what was your assignment given to you by the Red Cross? What did you do in that capacity in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Let me say that first of all, I would always come to the commissioner whose name was Ivica or Ivo Pandurevic and then he would inform me about everything that was going on in Zasavica. Then, the food shortage, he would say what was missing so that I could go back to the central Red Cross warehouse and bring that food.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, beforehand when we were discussing something, I would like to go back to part of your answer. You said that passes were needed in order to get in but also to get out, right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to go in and also to go out, but Croats for the most part were allowed to go out even without a pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What about the Muslims who were brought there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: They were put up in houses, in houses that were fabulous, fabulous rich houses, well equipped, well appointed, that's where they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could they leave or was their movement restricted?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I think their movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, could you please tell me what the living conditions were generally in Zasavica as compared to Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just in a couple of sentences, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to live now the way they lived at that time in Zasavica. If that's the proper answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain why?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: They had everything, good food, good accommodation, movement around the village, the only thing is perhaps that their freedom of movement outside was limited but everything else they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was Zasavica shelled at the time when those people were there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, Zasavica was never shelled, a shell never fell on Zasavica at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was there water?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was water. They had an artesian well, that was one of the best wells of that kind at the time in the whole of Posavina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has been informed that the laptop system is continuing to record so the proceedings can continue. The monitor in being looked into but if there will be any document on the ELMO it will show on the monitor if you press the right button, computer monitor. So Mr. Krgovic, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, could you please tell me just a couple of more things about Zasavica. Was there a health centre in Zasavica and did the detainees receive medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a place where the doctors would come. I would bring them to this place. I, myself, brought the doctors to this place that was allocated as the medical centre so if somebody was sick, the doctors would come and provide assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the International Red Cross ever visited Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they came to the village church. That's where all the people who wanted to come were to come and this is -- came and this is where they passed on messages to them and spoke to the population of Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, could you please tell me whether the citizens of Zasavica or those people, the Muslims who were from the town of Samac, applied wanting to go to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did apply to go to the other side. They applied to me and I would submit that list, that report to the president of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, I want to ask you about a few brief episodes, if you can clarify something for us. Do you know [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I didn't know him before that but I met him during the war. (redacted) .

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please now go into private session and if it's possible, could we erase the name of this person because in my notes now I see that this is a person who has already been mentioned in this case and I would like to explain that to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before we do, I can't see anything in the summary provided in relation to this specific person who's just been mentioned. There's a very general description of visits to Zasavica in relation to the exchanges. We certainly had no notice that this witness's evidence would be examined or questions would be asked about it, if that is indeed what my learned friend intends to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may say, I wrote the summary and the summary refers to certain facts that the witnesses will talk about during the entire proceedings. The Defence, of course, must contest the claims by the Prosecution so we did not understand that we need -- we didn't think that we would have to put in the summary facts which were mentioned by witnesses of the Prosecution and the witnesses who talk about individual episodes, the witnesses of the Prosecution, that -- there was nothing about that in that -- in the summaries either. We informed the Prosecution a few days ago that he would talk about episodes where he was mentioned as a participant but it's quite clear which witness was the one that talked about this witness but it's not something that we felt was necessary to put in the summary. I just need to mention one more thing about the summaries, Your Honours. My Defence and the other Defences in writing our summaries, we also thought about the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution and we often objected to much longer testimonies than was mentioned in the summary. So I believe that there is really no reason to overrule such questions if they refer to some things that the Prosecutor has claimed and of course they all are related to the actual exchanges and that is something that we have mentioned in the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will allow the Defence to proceed and discuss the allegation -- the specific allegations made by the -- some of the Prosecution witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Trial Chamber wishes to seek clarification on this name of, is it (redacted) ? He is not a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He's witness O, Your Honour. Witness O.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That's Witness O.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's Witness O. All right. Then the name will be redacted and we will use Witness O. Do you still want to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, do you know Jelena Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I do. Jelena Stanisic better said, but Jelena Kapetanovic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was she in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, did she tell you that she wanted to be exchanged? Did she apply to the list of persons who wanted to leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I have announced that we move into open session. I think it wasn't just picked up. In fact, we're already in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: We need the answer repeated, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, could you please repeat what I just asked you about whether she applied as wanting to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, do you know the persons from Zasavica [redacted] and Marta that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, [redacted] and Marta is the wife -- is the woman who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, did [redacted] and Marta offer you a certain amount of money, curtains and a canister of oil so that Jelena Kapetanovic could cross over to the other side to enable her to cross over and leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: That is a pure fabrication for somebody to sell themselves for a canister of gasoline or something like that, that is a pure fabrication, particularly because I don't believe that [redacted]would say anything like that because [redacted]is a very good person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, tell me, do you know Fadila Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear any answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters said they didn't hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, do you know Fadila Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On one occasion, when an exchange was organised, did she leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, Mrs. Fadila Drljacic, was she on the list of persons who could board the bus?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could it have happened or did it happen that she was not on the list and that you, on the spot, although she was not on the list, let her board the bus and cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No way, nor would I have allowed myself that kind of embarrassment or the people could say such things about me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Fadila Drljacic, did she give you a match box or something in which there was some gold, some valuables?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: She gave me a match box but this is the first time I hear that there was gold inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Why did she give you this?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: To have it crossed over -- to have it taken to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: To the destination where she would get off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Why did she give you this?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Out of sheer trust towards me because she knew that she would get it from me. Well that's it, she trusted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you return that match box to her?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: As soon as that border was crossed, immediately, out of my pocket straight into her hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the first time that somebody gave you valuables to take across or did you do that more often?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Well let me tell you now, the money I took across and the gold and jewellery I took across is an amount that you would not be able to believe, I mean I couldn't believe it myself, a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain this? Why did people give you money and gold to carry across for them, why did they not carry it themselves?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost they trusted me. Secondly, at the border crossing where we would come, there would be searches all kinds of searches with your indulgence may I say that they would look in places where nobody would ever look so they gave all this to me and I did it very gladly well to accommodate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who searched them?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: A person, a policeman, the police at the crossings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the crossings, which crossing do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I mean Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were there ever cases of the police taking away somebody's valuables, money or gold, did that ever happen?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I think that sometimes some women had 200 or 300 Deutschemark and they would take 200 Deutschemark from them and they would leave them only 100 Deutschemark or something like that. But that is what they had said to me, that's what they complained about but whether that's the way it was, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, did you ever take any kind of compensation for that, for making it possible for them to leave Samac by bus or through an exchange?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Never. Never. Let alone money, if I didn't give anything, I didn't take anything either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Miroslav Tadic ever took money from someone in order to place that person on the list of people who were going to be exchanged or to make it possible for such persons to leave Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No way. To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did people offer you money?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and how, and how and how, but I think that they were always mocked because they offered money and they were expelled from the office because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Vlado Zarka?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he offer money to you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes he did. Indeed. 1.000 Deutschemark or 1.500 Deutschemark I'm not sure, but 1.000 for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I threw him out, I said, "Give that money to whoever you can give it to and whoever can take you out." Those are my actual words and I said, "Don't ever come within my eyesight again."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, just one single brief question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Vasovic. I am attorney Lazarevic and on behalf of the Defence of Simo Zaric I'm going to put one single question to you. You said that you worked for the Red Cross and that on behalf of the Red Cross, you took part in the exchanges that were taking place. In this connection, did you have any contact with Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, never. Even when we would meet up, we didn't talk about any such thing, we only talked about private matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you attended the exchange itself, did you ever see Simo Zaric there?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: He was never there at the place where the exchanges were taking place or was he there where we were calling people's names out. I never noticed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, did he have any official position that had to do with exchanges?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, why would he? He was not a member of the Red Cross or anything like that so that he could influence exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Mr. Vasovic, I'm attorney Pantelic, Defence counsel for Dr. Blagoje Simic, I have just a few questions for you. You are probably tired. You mentioned that you've been a member of the socialist party for a long time now or actually before that you were a member of the league of communists of Yugoslavia and then of the SDP and now of the socialist party of Republika Srpska, tell me, in 1992, the SDP at local level, at the municipal parliament, did it take part, I mean was it in government in the echelons of power then?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was some maybe need some clarification in the transcript. In fact, I will clarify that with the witness very easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So your party was a parliamentary party at the level of the municipality of Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any representatives of your party in the municipal government, by that I mean the executive board, the executive authorities?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you are an educated person and you were involved in politics, in the course of 1992 and 1993, the local SDS at the level of Samac, did it ever promote a policy of persecuting the non-Serb population and expelling it from thee territory of the municipality of Samac, do you have any such knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I have not read their programme although all programmes are similar but I think and I claim that the SDS or any party never would have done any such thing as far as the persecution of the non-Serb population is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We are talking about Samac again. Did you ever hear that by way of some proclamation or by way of some public appearance, the SDS in Samac promoted the expulsion of non-Serbs from the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: There was no such thing. There really was no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you personally have any knowledge as to whether Dr. Blagoje Simic ever expressed any kind of discriminatory intention towards the non-Serbs in the territory of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was actually the other way around that he was tolerant towards everyone and that he behaved the same way to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. If Your Honour will just excuse me for one moment, I want to find something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, my name is David Re. I represent the Prosecution and I'm going to ask you some questions about your testimony and what happened in Samac in 1992 and 1993. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, you know Mr. Pantelic who is Dr. Simic's lawyer?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He just asked you about your political involvement. Now you stood for parliament, sorry, you stood as a candidate, didn't you, in October 1990 for the municipal elections on the SDP ticket; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you elected as a member of the municipal assembly on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you held political office since then?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Krgovic asked you about a nickname and you said that you had never had a nickname before.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Never, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, were you wearing -- did you wear glasses?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now the nickname that he asked you about "Obrva," that of course means "eyebrows," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's how it should be. If it's an eyebrow, yeah, that's what it is, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just take your glasses off for a moment and show the Trial Chamber your eyebrows, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is unjust to the witness and I really don't see the reason for these cheap moves by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes that will be struck off the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The showing of the eyebrows, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, you say that no one has called you that to your face, that's your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Never, I am sure. I would place my head on the line for that. I'm sure that I never heard that anybody called me by that nickname. I would put my head on the line right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about people saying it to you, you wouldn't of course know what people might have said about you behind your back, would you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I would find that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's been specific evidence in the case and Mr. Krgovic questioned the witness specifically on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes but he has denied that he ever was known by that nickname and right now it is emphatically denied again there is no point in going on about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not intending to go on about it, Your Honour, my only point is that he was visiting the -- the evidence about who called him Obrva was not someone who was his friend. It was someone in detention who said he came in. That's all. That's as far as I -- that's as far as I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And he wouldn't know, wouldn't necessarily know that someone else may have called him that, that's all. That's the only basis upon which I put that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you want to be helpful but you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But this is speculation. The question of the Prosecutor was would you know, would you have been able to know what people called you behind your back. That was actually the gist of my objection. He's asking the witness to speculate whether he could have known whether this is something that they called him behind his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I just asked him whether he would have known. That's different to speculating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If the question was did somebody ever tell you that you were being called by this name behind your back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is if someone had called you that behind your back, you wouldn't necessarily know, would you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah. You can put that question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I'm suggesting, Mr. Vasovic, is if someone called you Obrva behind your back, you wouldn't necessarily know, would you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Why not? I have so many friends and allow me to tell you I was much loved in the town of Samac as a teacher regardless of my ethnicity so I would find out everything. I have so many friends amongst Muslims and Croats and Serbs, you can't even understand how many friends I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Red Cross, of course, had a humanitarian role during the war in Samac and other places, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the Red Cross was concerned, who else would have any humanitarian role, if not the Red Cross, who else would be working on these humanitarian duties if not the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Red Cross structure within the Republika Srpska at the time, I just want to ask you about that. It was organised at a local and a national level, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the local and the national level depending on where it was formed and how it was formed -- no, I wouldn't say it was at the ethnic level, no, it wasn't -- it wasn't founded like that. Not even in Bosnia and Herzegovina was it formed along ethnic lines because there were Serbs and Croats there with whom I cooperated in the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this maybe a matter of translation, national level to this witness means ethnic level so this is how he understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, when I asked you the question a moment ago I wasn't suggesting it was formed along ethnic lines. I was talking about at a local, regional, and national in the sense of the country level.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you thought. I don't want to think about whether this was maybe ambiguous or not. I'm not sure what you are trying to get me to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Re you can rephrase your question and ask one question at a time at a local level, explain what you mean and then at the country's level, you explain what you mean. Let him answer the two questions separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic, I'm -- in order for the Trial Chamber to understand the role of your organisation, the Red Cross in Samac, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the organisation of the Red Cross at the local level, the regional level, and at the country level; do you understand that that's what I'm asking you about?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that at the local level, I explained that already, previously, what was being done at the local level. At the regional level, we cooperated, but I don't know about what was going on at a broader scale so why would I talk about something that I don't know. But I do know that there were Red Cross organisations in Muslim towns where they weren't the only ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please listen very carefully to the question. The question I asked you was: Do you understand that's what I'm asking you about. I wasn't asking you to go on, so please just listen to the question. What I want to ask you about is the structure from the bottom to the top of the Red Cross in the Republika Srpska at that time; do you understand that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. From the base, from the bottom, to the top, from the lowest structures up to the highest structures. Yes, that's how you meant, what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your evidence earlier was that you were formerly the president of the Bosanski Samac Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the municipality, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At that time was the Red Cross organised into local groups or branches that reported to a regional one?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course because the Red Cross, the municipal Red Cross existed, there was a Red Cross branch in every village with the local community which reported back about their work to the municipal Red Cross and then the municipal Red Cross reported back to the regional and so on. So what happened further along this line was something for others to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which group were you president of, was it a village Red Cross or a municipal Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: The municipal Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the municipal Red Cross work with the municipal authorities, that is the assembly and the government or the local government?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Only in providing reports of their work to them and about those things that other bodies were supposed to do to provide subsidies in order for the Red Cross to be able to provide assistance and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross -- sorry I'll start again. You just said the Red Cross reported to the local or the municipal government, did the Red Cross receive money from the municipal government?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, all the time. According to the annual plan of the municipal assembly, funds were allocated to the municipal Red Cross and the municipal Red Cross had then to decide how and where it would spend these funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the war, were you just referring to before the war; just yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: And before the war, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: During the war, did the Red Cross, the Red Cross which you were an activist in and worked very hard in during the war, did it continue to work with the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, because they also, on their own initiative, wanted to help the Red Cross so that they could do its job better because in the beginning, we didn't have enough food or other things so whatever they were able to, they gave to the Red Cross and this is something that you could have asked the president of the Red Cross Mihajlovic and also Velimir Maslic who was also here recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the Red Cross continued reporting to the municipal authorities during the war, that's after the 17th of April, 1992, did it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: In the initial period, no, not really. They worked -- on their own programme in their own way in the humanitarian aid area. We worked together with the centre for social work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your position or the position of the Red Cross allowed its members or activists to visit places such as detention centres that other people couldn't go to, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was the only one to visit all of those places on behalf of the Red Cross, the only person, all the places of detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's quarter to 6.00 Your Honour, is that the time for the break or is it 10 to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes we shall take our break now and continue at 1805 hours. --- Break taken at 5.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not able to continue our proceedings up to 19 hours, we've just been informed that due to the health concerns of the witness it's advisable that he takes a rest. So we will continue with him tomorrow. So we'll adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: at 6.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 31st day of January, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
